feasibility_assessment.coordinate_frame_gap: Bounding boxes [x1, y1, x2, y2] are in 2D camera image pixel coordinates. Because monocular dashcam focal lengths, pitch angles, and camera heights are uncalibrated, pixels cannot be transformed into physical metric (x, y) coordinates on the ground plane without introducing severe perspective errors.
feasibility_assessment.sampling_frequency_limitation: Keyframe sampling is 1.0 Hz (1 frame per second). Physical vehicle safety analysis, evasive maneuvers, and collision prediction require dense sampling (10 Hz, dt=0.1s). At 1 Hz, actors displace 5 to 15 metres between consecutive samples.
feasibility_assessment.tracking_continuity_gap: ByteTrack on monocular video in dense Indian traffic experiences frequent track fragmentation and ID switches during occlusions. Tracks lack dense continuous metric velocity vectors.
feasibility_assessment.ttc_calculation_invalidity: Physical Time-To-Collision (TTC) = separation_distance / relative_velocity. Computing TTC using pixel bounding box width or pixel rate-of-expansion violates projective geometry assumptions and produces unphysical, hazardous collision estimates.
feasibility_assessment.conclusion_and_role_in_project: The Indian Road Dataset serves as an essential descriptive reference for object class taxonomy (autorickshaws, unridden/ridden motorcycles, cattle/animals, pedestrians), informal traffic behavior, and visual scene context. Physical metric trajectory forecasting and collision-risk simulation must be executed using rigorous metric-coordinate synthetic environments.
